phases.name: Write the plan into the tracker

steps.name: Acceptance tests for TargetSheet.apply and a writing build (RED)
criteria: Everything the plan does not mention survives apply exactly: rows absent from the plan, blank-key hand-added rows, unknown columns in position and value, and every tab other than the plan's tab.
Human-owned cells in an updated row keep their values after apply.
Existing column order and existing row order are unchanged; appended columns go to the right of the header, appended rows go below the existing rows.
Numeric harvester values are written as numeric cells, not strings.

The write is atomic and bounded: after a successful apply the only file changed in the target directory is the target, and no temp file remains; if the write fails, the original target is byte-identical and no temp file remains.
apply returns a Receipt whose outputDigest is the sha256 of the file now on disk, and whose inputDigest is the sha256 of the file before the write.
build --out <t> --merge <t> merges into the tracker in place, and a human-typed Status survives it.
build --out <existing> without --merge refuses and leaves that file byte-identical, rather than overwriting a tracker it did not read.
build --out <absent> without --merge creates a new workbook.
A non-dry-run build refuses an empty cache and writes nothing.
A target failing its probe refuses the build and is left byte-identical.
Every new scenario is RED for the right reason — apply or the writing build is unimplemented — and the existing 118 still pass.
steps.scenario_name: apply lays the plan over the existing sheet and never loses what the plan does not mention
steps.implementation_notes: The central hazard: planMerge (src/core/merge.mjs) protects human data by OMISSION — rows absent from the harvest, blank-key rows, unknown columns, and every tab but Jobs never appear in the plan. The xlsx adapter cannot write individual cells (DR-0005 limitation 3, whole-tab rewrite), so an apply that builds the file from the plan alone deletes all of it. The tests must make that implementation impossible to pass. Pin DR-0004's invariants (every column has one owner; never delete a row; never match a blank key; never reorder columns). Do NOT try to pin DR-0005's named fidelity limitations — lost formatting, validation, notes, formulas re-evaluated — they are accepted, not guaranteed. Deterministic failure injection for atomicity: call apply directly on an existing readable target inside a 0o500 directory — reading succeeds, writing the sibling temp file fails with EACCES — and assert the original is byte-identical with no temp file left. Receipt persistence to .cache/receipts and the stale-upload warning (DR-0005 mitigation) are OUT OF SCOPE for this feature. Refreshing the Sources and Companies tabs on a merge build is OUT OF SCOPE: the plan covers one tab, so on merge they are preserved verbatim.

steps.name: Implement TargetSheet.apply and the writing build (GREEN)
criteria: All 18 scenarios in target-sheet-apply.test.mjs and build-writes-tracker.test.mjs pass, unmodified.
apply edits the existing worksheet's cells in place rather than regenerating the tab, so untouched cells keep their type and number format.
The workbook is read with cellNF: true, so date number formats survive; a human-typed Applied on Date stays a date.
Every tab other than the plan's is carried through as the original sheet object.
The write goes to a sibling temp file and is renamed over the target; on any failure the temp file is removed and the original error propagates.

build without --dry-run: refuses an empty cache; refuses an existing --out without --merge; refuses when --merge and --out differ; creates a new three-tab workbook when --out is absent; merges in place when --out equals --merge.
The full suite passes: 136 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (137).
Hand-check against a copy of the real tracker: every row survives, human-owned values are unchanged, and a date-formatted cell stays a date.
steps.scenario_name: apply lays the plan over the existing sheet and never loses what the plan does not mention
steps.implementation_notes: Tests reviewed by nw-acceptance-designer-reviewer (APPROVED WITH NOTES) and corrected twice: f155894 made the in-place merge scenario prove a write happened; 943f115 pinned date-format survival. MEASURED: SheetJS keeps a date number format only when read with {cellNF: true} AND the existing worksheet is edited in place — reading with defaults, or regenerating the tab via sheet_to_json/json_to_sheet, turns z:'dd/mm/yyyy' (14/09/2026) into z:'General' (46279) whichever read option is used. So apply must not rebuild the Jobs tab from rows.

steps.name: Make aDigestBody generate a card layout LinkedIn actually sends (GREEN)
criteria: aDigestBody produces, for every job it is given, a card that extractJobs reads back as exactly that job's title, company and location, in order.
A builder self-test pins that round trip for one job and for several, and is shown to fail against the previous builder.
The body still clears MINIMUM_DIGEST_BODY_LENGTH, with any padding placed where real LinkedIn mail puts filler — never inside a card's runs.
No assertion in any existing test changes.
The previously red scenario 'build --out <t> --merge <t> merges into the tracker in place' passes, and the full suite has 0 failures.
steps.scenario_name: a synthetic digest parses back to the jobs it was built from
steps.implementation_notes: Commit 126418a (write the merge plan) recorded the one remaining red scenario as 'a pre-existing card-boundary defect in src/core/parse-linkedin.mjs (cardFor)'. That diagnosis is WRONG and is corrected here. Measured across all 70 real messages (live cache + committed fixtures): zero 'Full-time · Hybrid · Posted N days ago' lines, zero '<Job> at <Co>: This is an excellent opportunity' description lines, zero blocks whose link run has >=3 prefix lines beneath a >=3-line card run. aDigestBody (padded in af9925c to clear the quarantine threshold) invents those lines inside the card's link run, so DR-0008's positional rule correctly takes the 4-line prefix as the card. The parser is right for every real shape; the builder is fiction. The in-place merge scenario is simply the first test to assert on Company from this builder — every other aMessage-based test has been extracting junk titles and passing because none checked. Fix the builder, not the parser.
